{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-nv-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"32d81685dbd3d4aac2fbe39b372bbaf820011e69720415abcd1fcd94a9198f37","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-nv-class-c:lineage:73","source_registry_sha256":"3e184808e042e052d0c78d0dff47c50b34a56560f428649c492afe10bc7ba712","source_liveness_sha256":"0dfbf3aa4b4798b88d69252e076642b5f0a38751c5010711fbce93c8a7d6e292"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Licensing confusables and document continuation facts","heading":"C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: validity periods, DAC versus license, Real ID versus standard, waiver versus vision test, and immigration and translation documents","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: validity periods, DAC versus license, Real ID versus standard, waiver versus vision test, and immigration and translation documents
Confusable pairs among licensing rules, followed by continuation facts on immigration documents, Real ID background, translations and residency forms; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec01-R01 | anchor: A01
Drivers sixty-five or older receive a four-year license instead of the eight-year term for applicants under sixty-five, unless limited-term immigration documents set a shorter expiration [A01].
Why it matters: group validity; confusable age-based license term versus ID card term.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R02 | anchor: A01
A driver license applicant must prove a Social Security Number if one was issued, but a Driver Authorization Card applicant needs no Social Security Number at all. [A01]
Why it matters: group credentials; confusable license versus DAC.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R03 | anchor: A02
The vision test is always given to a new resident, while the knowledge and road tests may be waived only when all of the transfer conditions hold. [A02]
Why it matters: group new residents; confusable always tested versus waivable.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R04 | anchor: A02
An active-duty service member needs only a valid home-state license, while a non-resident student, tourist or seasonal resident must also be at least 16 and follow Nevada traffic and financial responsibility laws. [A02]
Why it matters: group new residents; confusable military versus non-resident.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-R05 | anchor: A03
A Nevada Department of Corrections ID card proves name and birth date for a standard card but not for Real ID, while another state's limited-term Real ID proves neither. [A03]
Why it matters: group identity documents; confusable accepted-with-limits versus refused.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-R06 | anchor: A03
An old Resident Alien Card printed with no expiration date is accepted as a Permanent Resident Card; any other version of the Resident Alien Card is refused as proof of name, birth date or lawful status. [A03]
Why it matters: group identity documents; difficulty high.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-R07 | anchor: A03
The DMV will not force holders of the undated card to replace it unless DHS requests it, and the card rules may change with Department of Homeland Security policy. [A03]
Why it matters: group identity documents; difficulty high.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-R08 | anchor: A03
An expired I-94, whether with a permanent-resident passport stamp or with a US visa, must be paired with a Notice of Action (I-797) that shows an approved extension. [A03]
Why it matters: group identity documents; confusable expired I-94 rule applies to both groups.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-R09 | anchor: A03
Limited-term documents such as an Employment Authorization Card (I-766) produce a card marked Limited Term, and every immigration document is electronically checked for lawful status. [A03]
Why it matters: group identity documents; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-R10 | anchor: A04
A Real ID card has the gold Nevada outline and star cutout and meets federal standards, while a standard card says NOT FOR REAL ID PURPOSES and does not. [A04]
Why it matters: group Real ID; confusable Real ID versus standard.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-R11 | anchor: A04
Alternative identity documents can support a standard card with supervisory approval but are never accepted for a Real ID card. [A04]
Why it matters: group Real ID; confusable standard versus Real ID evidence.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-R12 | anchor: A04
The Real ID Act of May 2005 aims to fight terrorism, identity theft and other crimes by tightening the security of state-issued identification. [A04]
Why it matters: group Real ID; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-R13 | anchor: A04
A standard Nevada license holder who upgrades to Real ID must again show documents for name, birth date, Social Security Number and Nevada residential address, and they may be scanned, stored and electronically verified. [A04]
Why it matters: group Real ID; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-R14 | anchor: A05
A Driver Authorization Card works like a license for driving and follows the same rules unless the handbook says otherwise, yet it cannot serve as identification for any federal or state purpose. [A05]
Why it matters: group credentials; misconception DAC equals ID.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-R15 | anchor: A05
Translated documents must cover the entire original, be typed or printed electronically, and carry a signed statement in which the translator certifies the translation is complete and accurate and that they are fluent in both languages. [A05]
Why it matters: group documents; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-R16 | anchor: A06
The three department-approved residency forms are the Relief Agency or Shelter Certification (DMV 115), the Property Owner Residency Affidavit (DMV 116) and the Certification of Nevada Residency (DMV 005). [A06]
Why it matters: group residency; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-R17 | anchor: A06
A notarized statement from the owner of the home saying the applicant physically lives there is one of the listed residency documents, as is a voter registration card from a county clerk or the county registrar of voters. [A06]
Why it matters: group residency; difficulty low.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0011]
